Get started

Introduction

Meet Jev, TypeSafe’s System One model. Provide your data and a set of typed questions, then use the answers directly in your application.

Language models are useful when the output you need is text. An application often needs something narrower: a category, a score, or a decision it can act on. Turning generated prose into those values adds another step between the model and your software.

Jev takes a different approach. A System One model evaluates questions about the state you supply and produces structured answers. Your application receives values and probabilities it can use for branching, ranking, and routing. Where supported, confidence helps your code choose how to handle an answer.

TypeSafe primitives

Choose the answer shape your application needs. Each primitive defines a different kind of judgment.

Question typeGoalReturns
ChoiceSelect an optionchoice, probabilities, confidence
ScoreApply a scoring rubricscore, probabilities, confidence
NoulEvaluate a statementnoul (0–1)

Atomic questions, composed in code

Keep questions focused. Break a larger decision into individual judgments, then combine their results in your code. This makes the application’s decision rules explicit and easy to adjust.
